articles.title: Newborn Sleep Schedule: Tips for a Restful Night'
articles.excerpt: Has your baby confused night and day? Discover newborn sleep cycles, the role of melatonin, and golden rules for putting your baby to sleep. A complete guide to white noise, swaddling, and safe sleep environments.
articles.content:
The sentence parents use most in the first weeks after returning from the maternity hospital is probably this: *"I am so tired"*. Waking up in the middle of the night, rocking the baby for hours, and starting the morning like a "zombie"... Welcome to the world of parenting\!

The sleep schedule (or rather, the lack of it) of newborns is a real test for adults. Some babies spend the day like "sleeping beauty" and turn the nights into a real party. So how can this mess be sorted out? How to teach a baby the idea that "night is for sleeping"?

In this article, we have gathered methods to help you understand your baby's sleep biology and gain calmer nights for both of you.Accept the Reality: The Baby Has No "Clock"

First, you must accept one truth: the "Biological Clock" (Circadian rhythm) has not yet formed in the brain of a newborn baby (0-3 months).  - **Lack of Melatonin:** The sleep hormone melatonin is not yet produced in the baby's body. They cannot distinguish between the darkness of night and the light of day.
  - **Short Cycles:** Although babies sleep 16-18 hours a day, this sleep is divided into short 2-4 hour segments. The reason is simple: their stomachs are very small and they get hungry often.That is, a baby waking up at night in the first months is an indicator of **completely normal and healthy** development. However, this does not mean you cannot make the process a little easier.How to Teach Day and Night?

If your baby confuses night with day (sleeping during the day and staying awake at night), it is in your hands to explain the difference:Day Routine: "Noise and Light"  - Open the curtains, let the room be bright.
  - Continue with daily household noises (vacuum cleaner, TV, talking). Do not speak in whispers.
  - When the baby is awake, play with them, talk to them, and ensure they expend energy.Night Routine: "Silence and Darkness"  - Dim the lights in the house after sunset.
  - **Do not turn on the light** during night feedings (use a dim night lamp).
  - Do not make eye contact or play with the baby. Do your job (feeding, changing the diaper) quietly and quickly.
  - This will signal to the baby that "now is not playtime, it is sleep time."4 Golden Rules for Putting Your Baby to Sleep Comfortably1. Swaddling – Return to the Womb

Babies suddenly throw their arms and wake themselves up in their sleep due to the "Moro reflex" (startle reflex).  - **Solution:** Swaddling the baby with a thin cloth (without squeezing too tightly) reminds them of the tightness in the mother's womb and prevents startling. This is the most effective method to prolong sleep duration.2. White Noise

The mother's womb was not silent at all (blood flow, heartbeat). Total silence makes the baby uncomfortable.  - **Solution:** Hairdryer sounds, rain sounds, or special "white noise" applications (available in the **Anacan app**) calm the baby and help them fall into a deep sleep.3. Sleep Rituals (Routine)

Doing the same actions every evening gives the baby the "it's time to sleep" message.  - **Example:** Warm bath -\> Light massage -\> Putting on pajamas -\> Lullaby or White noise -\> Feeding -\> Sleep. Do this in the same order every night.4. "Sleepy but Awake" Principle

This is the most important habit for the future. Put the baby in their bed not after they have fallen completely asleep, but while they are sleepy and drowsy. This way, they will learn to fall asleep in their bed and will be able to go back to sleep on their own when they wake up at night.Safe Sleep Rules (Against SIDS Risk)

The baby's safety is as important as their comfort. To reduce the risk of Sudden Infant Death Syndrome (SIDS), be sure to follow these rules:  - **Always on the back:** Never put the baby to sleep face down (on their tummy). This is the safest position.
  - **Empty bed:** There should be no pillows, blankets, soft toys, or bumpers in the crib. Only a firm mattress and a fitted sheet.
  - **Temperature:** The room temperature should be 20-22°C. Do not overdress the baby (the back of their neck should be warm, they should not sweat).Dear parents, sleepless nights may seem endless, but believe me, this is temporary. As your baby grows (especially after the 3rd-4th month), their sleep will become regular and they will start producing melatonin themselves.

Be patient, support each other, and try to sleep when your baby sleeps (housework can wait!).

**Want to track your baby's sleep?** Record your baby's sleep intervals with the **"Sleep Tracker" in the Anacan app** and understand their routine better.

articles.title: Gas (Colic) Problems in Babies: Massage Techniques and Methods to Relieve Pain
articles.excerpt: Is your baby crying inconsolably? Learn what colic (gas pains) is and when it passes. Discover ways to soothe your baby with "I Love You" massage, bicycle leg exercises, white noise, and feeding tips.
articles.content:
The first days you come home with your newborn baby, everything seems perfect. But about 2-3 weeks later, those "unexplained" crying spells begin, usually starting in the evening and lasting for hours. You feed them, change their diaper, hold them – nothing helps. The baby pulls their legs up to their stomach, their face turns red, and they seem to be in great pain.

Welcome to the world of **Colic**.

This situation can be a real nightmare for parents. It is completely normal to feel helpless and exhausted. But remember: Colic is not a disease; it is the development process of the baby's digestive system and it is *temporary*.

In this article, we have gathered the most effective massage techniques and proven methods for you to alleviate your baby's pain and restore peace to your home.What is Colic? The "Rule of 3s"

Doctors use the famous **"rule of 3s"** to diagnose colic:  - The baby cries for at least **3 hours** a day.
  - This occurs at least **3 days** a week.
  - And it continues for more than **3 weeks**.Colic usually starts at 2-3 weeks of age, peaks at the 6th week, and disappears on its own (miraculously!) at 3-4 months.3 Best Massage Techniques to Relieve Gas

Massage is the most natural way to move gas in the baby's tummy and relax the intestines. The massage should be done when the baby is calm (before a crying fit) or at least 30-40 minutes after a feeding.Preparation: Warm your hands and use a little baby oil (or olive oil).1. "I Love You" Massage

This is the most popular colic massage in the world. It helps the intestines work in a clockwise direction. The baby lies on their back:  - **"I":** Draw a straight line from under the ribs down to the hip on the left side (the baby's left side from your perspective) (the letter "I").
  - **"L":** Starting from the right side, draw an inverted "L" across the top of the belly to the left and then down.
  - **"U":** Starting from the right hip, draw an inverted "U" up, across to the left, and down.
    Repeat this 5-10 times and say "I love you" to the baby each time.2. Bicycle Legs

The baby lies on their back. Hold their legs and move them gently as if they are riding a bicycle. Then push both knees toward the belly and hold for 3-5 seconds. This movement greatly helps the gas to be expelled (farting).3. Clockwise (Sun and Moon)

Using the palm of your hand, make circular motions around the baby's navel in a clockwise direction. This follows the natural flow of the digestive system and moves gas bubbles along the intestines.Other Ways to Soothe the Pain

In addition to massage, try these methods to calm the baby:"Tiger in the Tree" Hold

Hold the baby face down, with their belly resting on your forearm. Rest their head in the crook of your elbow and hold between their legs with your hand. In this position, light pressure is applied to the belly, which reduces the cramp. Walk around the house in this position.Warm Compress

Place a warm (not hot\!) towel or an ironed cotton cloth on the baby's belly. **Cherry pit bags** sold in pharmacies are also an excellent tool as they retain heat for a long time. Heat relaxes the muscles.White Noise

Inside the womb, the baby heard constant noise. Complete silence can make them feel uneasy. The sound of a hair dryer, vacuum cleaner, or special "white noise" apps (available in the **Anacan app**) can miraculously calm the baby.Swaddling

Swaddling the baby's arms and legs close to their body reminds them of the tightness and sense of security in the womb. This is effective for stopping crying fits.Nutrition: What to Watch Out For?  - **Breastfeeding mothers:** Some foods the mother eats (cabbage, chickpeas, beans, cow's milk, chocolate) can cause gas in the baby. Remove the food you suspect from your diet and monitor the results.
  - **Formula (Smes):** If the colic is very severe, consult your doctor about switching to "Anti-colic" or "Comfort" series formulas. Also, using an **anti-colic bottle** prevents the baby from swallowing air.Is Medication Necessary?

Products containing simethicone (Espumisan, Bobotik, etc.) or dill water are sold in pharmacies.  - **The Truth:** These medications can help break down gas bubbles, but they may not be 100% effective since the main cause of colic is the immaturity of the nervous system. Do not give medication without consulting your doctor.Dear parents, I know your heart breaks when your baby cries and it feels like these days will never end. But believe me, this is just a phase. After 3-4 months, you will forget these difficult days and enjoy your baby's smiles.

Be patient, support each other, and do not get tired of massaging.

**White Noise and Logs:**
Access the "White Noise" library to calm your baby and the **Anacan app** to log crying times.

articles.title: Breastfeeding Guide: Proper Techniques and Tips to Increase Milk Supply
articles.excerpt: Why is breast milk low? What to eat to increase milk supply? Correct breastfeeding positions, nutrition for nursing mothers, and tips to end the fear of "not having enough milk."
articles.content:
Do you remember that moment when you first held your baby in your arms? Those tiny hands, those searching eyes... Nature has thought of everything for this moment: your body produces the most perfect food for your baby – **Breast Milk**.

Breast milk is not just food; it is also the baby's first vaccine. It is full of live cells, antibodies, and hormones. However, let's admit that the breastfeeding process does not always start as easily and romantically as in the movies. Questions like *"Is the baby latching correctly?", "Is my milk enough?", "Why does it hurt?"* often worry new mothers.

In this article, we will explore the secrets of successful breastfeeding, scientific ways to increase milk supply, and how true our grandmothers' advice to "drink sweet tea for milk" actually is.1. Correct Breastfeeding: Everything starts with the "Latch"

The most important condition for painless and effective breastfeeding is the baby's correct grasp of the breast (**Latching**). If you feel severe pain during breastfeeding or if sores develop on your nipples, it means there is an error in the latch.

**Signs of a correct latch:**  - **Wide mouth:** The baby's mouth should be wide open (like a "fish mouth") and should grasp not only the nipple but also the brown area around it (the areola).
  - **Chin contact:** The baby's chin should firmly touch your breast, while the nose should be free.
  - **Lips:** The baby's bottom lip should be curled outward.
  - **Sound:** You should hear the baby's swallowing sound, not a "clicking" sound (if there is clicking, it means they are swallowing air).Advice: Before starting to breastfeed, choose a comfortable place for yourself. Place pillows under your back and arm. If you are not comfortable, the flow of milk (oxytocin reflex) may become difficult.2. The "My milk is low" fear and ways to increase milk supply

Many mothers suspect their milk is low and hastily switch to artificial formula. However, remember: milk production works on the principle of **"Demand and Supply."** The more the baby sucks, the more the signal "more milk is needed" goes to the brain, and the body produces more milk.

**The most effective ways to increase milk supply:**Breastfeed frequently

Breastfeed a newborn baby whenever they want, not by the clock. It is normal to breastfeed 8-12 times (or more) a day. Night feedings are especially important because the milk hormone (prolactin) is secreted more at night."Skin-to-skin" contact

Place the baby naked (with a diaper) on your chest and cover yourselves with a blanket. This contact increases the oxytocin hormone for both you and the baby and makes it easier for the milk to come.Empty the breasts completely

Do not move to the other breast before the baby has completely emptied one. The milk at the end of the feeding (**hindmilk**) is fattier and more satiating.Drink plenty of water

87% of breast milk consists of water. If you stay dehydrated, your milk may decrease. Place a glass of water next to you during every breastfeeding session.3. Nutrition: "Lactogenic" foods

Even though our grandmothers say "eat halva, drink sweet tea," sugar does not increase milk; it only causes weight gain. Foods that increase milk (galactagogues) include:  - **Fennel and Cumin:** Drinking them brewed as tea both increases milk and reduces the baby's gas (colic).
  - **Oatmeal:** Eating oatmeal for breakfast is an excellent choice.
  - **Walnuts, Hazelnuts, Almonds:** They are sources of Omega-3 and protein, increasing the quality of the milk.
  - **Dates:** They are a source of natural energy and vitamins.
  - **Green leafy vegetables:** Spinach, dill, parsley.4. Popular myths about breastfeedingMyth: "My milk is thin, like water; the baby isn't getting full."
Fact: Breast milk is never of poor quality. The milk that comes at the beginning of a feeding (foremilk) is watery to quench the baby's thirst. As breastfeeding continues, the milk becomes thicker and fattier (hindmilk). Therefore, do not cut the breastfeeding session short.Myth: "My breasts are small; I will have little milk."
Fact: Breast size depends on fatty tissue, while the number of mammary glands is approximately the same in every woman. It is possible to satisfy twins even with small breasts\!Myth: "Stress cuts off the milk."
Fact: Strong stress does not stop milk production, but it can make the flow of milk (the let-down reflex) difficult. Once you calm down and smell your baby, the milk will come again.How to know if the baby is full?

Crying does not always mean hunger. You can tell if your baby is full by these two indicators:1.  **Dirty diapers:** After the 5th day, if the baby urinates at least 5-6 times a day (the diaper gets heavy) and the stool color is yellow.
2.  **Weight gain:** The baby should regain the weight lost in the first week by days 10-14 and then continue to gain weight steadily.Breastfeeding is a process that requires patience and experience. Even if the first days are difficult, do not give up. Every drop of breast milk is the most precious gift you give to your baby. If you are having difficulty, consult your pediatrician or a breastfeeding consultant.

To record breastfeeding times, the baby's dirty diapers, and sleep, you can use the **"Baby Tracker"** function in the **Anacan app**.

articles.title: Newborn Baby Care: Everything You Need to Know (Bathing and Cord Care)
articles.excerpt: First days home after the maternity hospital: How to care for a baby's umbilical cord? Rules for the first bath, diaper changes, and skin care. A step-by-step guide for young mothers.
articles.content:
The moment you leave the maternity hospital and enter your home with that little "bundle" in your arms... This is both the happiest and most terrifying moment in the world. The nurses at the hospital did everything, but what now? The baby looks so small and delicate that you are even afraid to touch them. Questions like "Will I hurt their belly button?", "Is the water too hot?", or "Did I dress them correctly?" swirl in your mind.

Dear mother (and father), stay calm. Babies are more resilient than you think. In this article, we will explain the basic knowledge you will need most in the first days—hygiene, bathing, and umbilical cord care—in simple and clear language.1. Umbilical Cord Care: Don't be afraid to touch!

The umbilical cord stump of a newborn is the part that worries parents the most. It usually dries up and falls off on its own 10-21 days after birth. Until then, the main rule is to **"Keep it Clean and Dry"**.Golden Rules:  - **Do not apply alcohol or Zelyonka (Brilliant Green):** Modern pediatrics does not recommend this. These substances can burn the skin and delay the healing process. Wiping with just boiled water and sterile gauze is sufficient.
  - **Fasten the diaper below the navel:** Fold the edge of the diaper so the umbilical cord remains exposed to the air. Air exposure speeds up the drying process.
  - **Bathing is allowed:** You can bathe the baby before the umbilical cord falls off; just make sure to dry that area carefully and completely after the bath.Warning Signs (When to call the doctor?):  - If there is redness and swelling around the navel.
  - If there is a foul-smelling or purulent discharge.
  - If the baby cries when the navel is touched.2. The First Bath: Introduction to Water

You don't need to bathe your baby every day (2-3 times a week is enough), but in our culture, a daily wash (especially in the evenings before sleep) is a tradition and is beneficial for calming the baby.Preparation:

The room temperature should be **24-26°C**, and the water temperature should be **37°C** (body temperature). To check the water temperature, dip your elbow into the water—it should be neither hot nor cold.Step-by-Step:1.  **Safety:** Keep all supplies (towel, soap, diaper) within reach. Never leave the baby alone in the water\!
2.  **Slowly:** Do not plunge the baby into the water suddenly. Lower the feet first, then the body. Support the head and neck with your arm.
3.  **Face and Head:** Wash the face with clean water without soap. Wipe the eyes from the inside out. Wash the head with a special baby shampoo (tear-free).
4.  **Body:** Don't forget to wash the armpits, neck folds, and between the fingers.Myth: "Salt should be added to the water until the baby is forty days old."
Truth: Salty water can dry out and irritate the baby's delicate skin. Regular tap water (if clean) or boiled water is best.3. Diaper Changes and Preventing "Diaper Rash"

A baby's skin is very sensitive. Diaper rash occurs when moisture and stool stay in contact with the skin for a long time.  - **Change frequently:** Change the baby's diaper every 2-3 hours or immediately after every bowel movement.
  - **Wash, don't wipe:** Whenever possible, wash the baby's bottom under running water instead of using wet wipes. Wipes (even the most expensive ones) can cause irritation.
  - **Air bath:** Before putting on a new diaper, leave the baby's bottom uncovered for 5-10 minutes so the skin can breathe.
  - **Cream:** Use protective creams containing zinc (Sudocrem, Desitin, etc.). The use of powder (talc) is no longer recommended (it can enter the respiratory tract).4. Skin Care: Peeling and Rashes

In the first weeks, you may see peeling (flaking) or small pimples on the baby's skin.  - **Peeling:** This is normal. The baby has been in water for 9 months and is now coming into contact with air. You can apply moisturizing baby oil or lotion.
  - **Hormonal Acne:** Small red rashes (neonatal acne) may appear on the face. This is related to hormones passed from the mother and clears up on its own without requiring treatment. Do not squeeze them\!5. Ears, Nose, and Nails  - **Ears:** Never insert a cotton swab into the ear canal\! Just wipe the outside.
  - **Nose:** Nasal congestion prevents the baby from sucking. You can clean it with sea water drops and an aspirator.
  - **Nails:** Babies tend to scratch their own faces. Cut their nails with special baby scissors while they are sleeping. You can use mittens for the first few days.The first days may seem difficult, but believe me, your hands will get used to it very quickly. You are the best specialist for your baby. Trust your instincts and don't hesitate to ask for help (from your spouse, your mother).

Download the **Anacan app** to track your baby's sleep schedule, nutrition, and weight gain. We are with you during your first year\!

articles.title: Fear of Childbirth (Tokophobia): Expert Tips on How to Overcome It
articles.excerpt: What is tokophobia (fear of childbirth)? 5 psychological techniques to overcome fear during pregnancy. A guide for mothers afraid of pain, complications, or C-sections.
articles.content:
As the final days of pregnancy approach, many women feel more anxiety than joy. They stay awake at night, read "scary birth stories" on the internet, and replay the same scenarios in their minds: *"What if I can't do it?", "Will I be able to stand the pain?", "Will something happen to my baby?"*.

Dear future mother, you must know that you are not alone. It is completely normal to be afraid of childbirth. However, if this fear reaches a level that paralyzes your life, it may be a medical condition – **Tokophobia**.

In this article, we will delve into the roots of the fear of childbirth and learn ways to turn this fear into confidence with 5 effective methods recommended by psychologists.What is Tokophobia? Difference from normal anxiety

Every pregnant woman experiences some anxiety regarding the birth process. This is the "fear of the unknown" and it is natural. However, **Tokophobia** is a pathological (extreme) fear.  - **Symptoms:** Panic attacks, nightmares, increased heart rate when thinking about birth, crying spells, and even persistently demanding a cesarean section due to this fear.3 main sources of fear

To face your fear, you must first name it. What do you fear the most?1.  **Fear of pain:** "There will be unbearable pain, I will die".
2.  **Fear of losing control:** "I won't be able to control my body, the doctors won't listen to me".
3.  **Fear of trauma:** "There will be tearing, my health will be ruined".5 Psychological Techniques to overcome fear1. Maintain an "Information Diet"

In our society, women love to tell exaggerated stories of difficult births to prove their "heroism".  - **Advice:** Stop listening to negative stories. When your friend starts with "I was in labor for 20 hours...", politely interrupt her: *"Please, I only need positive stories"*. Feed your brain with successful and calm birth stories, not scary scenarios.2. Use the power of knowledge

Humans fear what they do not know most. Learn the physiology of the birth process.  - **Fact:** A contraction (surge) is not meant to cause pain, but to open the cervix. Every contraction is a "labor force" bringing you closer to your baby.
  - **Action:** Go to birth preparation courses or watch birth videos in the **Anacan app**. Knowing the process step-by-step will give you a sense of control.3. Replace the word "Pain" with "Power" (Hypnobirthing)

Our language shapes our thoughts. Instead of saying to yourself "Unbearable pain is coming", say "A strong wave is coming".  - **Technique:** Instead of tensing your body when a contraction comes (which increases pain), try to relax. Take a deep breath and imagine that with every exhale, the tension in your body flows away into water.4. Build a "Bridge of Trust" with your doctor

Do not hide your fears from your doctor. Tell them, "I am very afraid". A good doctor will take your feelings seriously and calm you down.  - **Discussion:** Discuss pain relief options (Epidural anesthesia) in advance. Knowing that pain can be managed will give you peace of mind.5. Prepare a Birth Plan (But be flexible)

Planning what will happen at the hospital reduces stress.  - Who will be with you? (Your partner, your mother?).
  - Do you want to listen to music?
  - Should the lights be dimmed?
    Thinking about these small details will shift your focus away from fear and toward a sense of "nesting".When is professional help needed?

If your fears interfere with your daily life, disrupt your sleep and appetite, be sure to see a perinatal psychologist. A few sessions of therapy can help untie this knot.

Childbirth is the most natural and powerful function of the female body. Your body is programmed to do this job. Millions of women have succeeded, and you will too.

Fear is normal, but do not let it overshadow the most beautiful day of your life. Take a deep breath, think of your baby, and say to yourself: *"I am strong, I can do this\!"*.

**To calm down:** You can manage your stress throughout pregnancy by using the "Meditation and Breathing Exercises" section in the **Anacan app**.

articles.title: Water Breaking and Bloody Show during Pregnancy: 3 Main Signs of Labor
articles.excerpt: How to know when labor starts? When does the mucus plug (bloody show) pass? How to distinguish between water breaking and urinary incontinence? Key signs indicating when to go to the hospital.
articles.content:
In the final days of pregnancy, every mother-to-be feels as if she is at the "start line." The bags are packed, the nursery is ready, but the main question remains unanswered: *"How will I know when labor has started?"*.

In movies, everything is usually dramatic: a woman's water suddenly breaks like a "flood" and she immediately begins to experience contractions. However, in real life, the scenario can be different. Sometimes the process starts with small signs that last for days. The most confusing of these signs is the difference between the **"Bloody Show"** and **"Water Breaking."**

In this article, we will explain how to correctly read the signals your body is sending you and when to hurry and when to wait calmly.1. What is the Bloody Show (Mucus Plug)?

Throughout pregnancy, the cervix is closed with a thick, jelly-like layer of mucus (**plug**) to protect the fetus from infections. As birth approaches, the cervix softens, shortens, and begins to open. At this time, that plug detaches and is discharged.

**What does the bloody show look like?**  - **Color:** It can be clear, white, pink, or brown (mixed with blood).
  - **Consistency:** It is sticky and stringy, similar to egg white.
  - **Amount:** It may come out as a whole piece at once, or in parts over several days.**What to do if the bloody show appears?**
Do not panic or hurry. The appearance of the bloody show does not mean labor has started, but simply that it is **approaching**. Labor may still be a few hours, or even **several days or weeks** away.  - **Action plan:** Continue with your daily life. Monitor whether contractions have started.2. What is Water Breaking (Amniotic Fluid)?

Your baby lives inside a water-filled balloon called the "amniotic sac." When labor starts (or sometimes before it starts), this sac ruptures and the water flows out.

**How to recognize water breaking?**
It is not always an "explosion" like in the movies.  - **Leaking:** Often, the water just leaks drop by drop. Women often mistake this for urinary incontinence (which is normal at the end of pregnancy).
  - **Flow:** In rare cases, water can come down your legs in a strong flow.**Urine or Water? Test it:**1.  Go to the toilet and empty your bladder.
2.  Put on a dry pad and cough or lie down and get up.
3.  If the fluid continues to come and you cannot hold it with your muscles, it is most likely **amniotic fluid**.**Color and smell of the water:**  - **Normal:** It is clear or straw-yellow in color. It is odorless or has a slight sweet smell (it does not smell like ammonia like urine).
  - **Dangerous:** If the water is **green or brown**, it indicates that the baby has passed stool (meconium) into the water. In this case, it is necessary to inform the doctor immediately.Main Differences: Summary Table| Sign           | Bloody Show (Plug)            | Water Breaking                    |
| :------------- | :---------------------------- | :-------------------------------- |
| **Appearance** | Thick, stringy, jelly-like    | Thin, watery                      |
| **Color**      | Pink, brown, bloody           | Clear, yellowish                  |
| **Urgency**    | Can wait (if no contractions) | **To the hospital immediately\!** |
| **Meaning**    | Cervix is opening             | Protective barrier is broken      |
When to go to the hospital?

The reaction to these two events should be different:1.  **If only the Bloody Show has appeared:** Stay at home. Wait for contractions to start or the water to break. Check your bag, take a shower, relax.
2.  **If the Water has broken (even if there are no contractions):** Go to the **hospital** without losing time.
      - **Reason:** After the water sac ruptures, the baby remains defenseless against infections. Doctors usually want the birth to take place within 24 hours after the water breaks.
      - **Attention:** If the water has broken, do not take a bath (a shower is okay) and do not have sexual intercourse.The Golden Rule: 5-1-1

If the water hasn't broken, the bloody show has appeared, and contractions have started, wait for the **"5-1-1"** rule to go to the hospital:  - Contractions come every **5 minutes**.
  - Each contraction lasts for **1 minute**.
  - This rhythm continues for **1 hour**.The bloody show means "get ready," and the water breaking means "set off." Your body signals the arrival of your baby with these signs. Do not be afraid; nature has planned everything perfectly.

Use the **Anacan app** to track your contractions and check the hospital bag list. Have a safe delivery\!

articles.title: Epidural Anesthesia (Painless Birth): Benefits and Side Effects
articles.excerpt: What is epidural anesthesia and how does it eliminate labor pains? Answers to scary questions like "Does the needle stay in the back?" and "Is there a risk of paralysis?" Everything about the benefits, side effects, and cost of painless childbirth.
articles.content:
When thinking about birth throughout pregnancy, many women's greatest fear is pain. The question *"Will I be able to endure the contractions?"* sometimes even overshadows the feeling of joy. Fortunately, modern medicine offers us an opportunity like **Epidural anesthesia** (popularly known as the "Prophet's needle" or "Painless birth").

However, there are so many myths surrounding this topic – "back pain remains," "you will be paralyzed," "it harms the baby" – that women have difficulty choosing. Let's explore what this procedure actually is, how it works, and its risks with medical facts.How does epidural anesthesia work?

Epidural anesthesia is a regional numbing method that blocks the sensation of pain in a specific part of the body (below the navel).

**How is the procedure performed?**1.  You sit or lie on your side (you should arch your back "like a cat").
2.  The anesthesiologist numbs your lower back area (this is the needle you will feel the most).
3.  Without entering the spinal canal, a very thin catheter (plastic tube) is placed simply into the **epidural space**.
4.  The needle is removed, only the soft catheter remains, and the medication is administered through it.As a result, you feel the contractions (tightening) as pressure, but you **do not feel pain**. You remain conscious, can move (depending on the dose), and participate actively in the birth.Advantages: Why should you choose it?1.  **Painless birth:** This is the biggest advantage. You are freed from the stress and fatigue caused by contractions. You save your energy for pushing the baby (the second stage of labor) rather than for screaming.
2.  **Calming:** When pain decreases, the level of adrenaline in your body drops, which can help the cervix open more easily.
3.  **Emergency Cesarean possibility:** If a sudden problem arises during birth and a C-section is needed, there is no need for general anesthesia. The dose of medication is simply increased through the catheter.
4.  **Beneficial for hypertension:** Epidural anesthesia helps lower high blood pressure, which is beneficial for mothers at risk of preeclampsia.Disadvantages and Side Effects

Every medical intervention has risks, but epidural risks are rare and usually manageable.  - **Drop in blood pressure:** This is the most common occurrence. Since doctors know this in advance, they give you an IV (fluids) and keep your pressure under control.
  - **Prolongation of labor:** In some cases, an epidural may slightly prolong the second stage of labor (pushing), as you may not know when to push because you do not feel the contraction. Your doctor will guide you.
  - **Headache:** Very rarely (less than 1%), if the needle accidentally punctures the spinal fluid sac, there may be a severe headache after birth. This is treatable.
  - **Numbness in the legs:** You may feel heaviness or numbness in your legs for a few hours after birth.Myths and TruthsMyth: "Epidural causes paralysis."
Truth: This is almost impossible. The needle is not inserted into the spinal cord (where the nerves are), but is placed at a considerable distance from it.Myth: "Back pain remains for life."
Truth: There may be slight sensitivity at the needle site for 1-2 days. However, if your back hurts months after birth, the reason is not the needle, but the shift in the center of gravity during pregnancy and carrying the baby in your arms.Myth: "The medication passes to the baby and numbs them."
Truth: The amount of epidural drugs absorbed into the blood is very small and has no serious effect on the baby. Babies are usually born alert.When should it be administered?

Epidural anesthesia is administered when labor contractions become regular and the cervix is dilated **3-4 cm**. If administered too early, it can slow down labor; if administered too late (at full dilation), it may no longer be meaningful.How much does it cost?

It is free in state hospitals if there is a medical indication (but it is usually used for C-sections). In private clinics, an additional payment of approximately **100-200 AZN** may be required in addition to the natural birth package.

Epidural anesthesia is not about avoiding heroism, but about using the comfort created by modern medicine. If your pain threshold is low or you simply want to enjoy the birth and experience that first moment without pain, consider this choice.

Talk to an anesthesiologist and share your fears before making a decision. You can get more realistic information by reading the epidural experiences of other mothers in the **Anacan app**.

articles.title: Natural Birth vs. C-Section: Indications, Benefits, and Risks
articles.excerpt: What are the benefits of natural birth and the risks of a C-section? In which cases is surgery mandatory? A comparative guide on recovery, fear of pain, and the healthiest choice for the baby.
articles.content:
As the final months of pregnancy approach, the question that occupies the minds of future mothers most is: *"How will I give birth? Naturally, or by cesarean section?"*. In recent years, the number of cesarean sections in Azerbaijan has increased significantly. Many women see the surgery as an "easy way" because they fear labor pains. On the other hand, there are many who remain under pressure from elders saying, "Natural birth is the best."

But where does the truth lie? Which choice is safer for both you and your baby? Let's weigh the medical aspects, advantages, and risks of both methods.Natural Birth: Nature's "Gold Standard"

The female body has evolved over centuries for the process of childbirth. If there is no medical obstacle, the World Health Organization (WHO) recommends natural birth.Advantages:1.  **Faster recovery:** You can stand up, hold your baby, and eat a few hours after birth. The hospital stay is short (1-2 days).
2.  **Benefits for the baby:** As the baby passes through the birth canal, the fluid in their lungs is squeezed out, making it easier for them to breathe. Also, they acquire a strong immunity by receiving the mother's beneficial bacteria (microbiota).
3.  **Lactation:** The arrival of milk and the breastfeeding process usually starts earlier and more comfortably.
4.  **No surgical risk:** The abdominal cavity is not opened, which reduces the risk of infection and bleeding.Disadvantages and Risks:  - **Pain:** Contractions are painful (but it is possible to minimize the pain with modern **Epidural anesthesia**).
  - **Unpredictability:** It is impossible to know in advance how long the labor will last (5 hours or 20 hours).
  - **Tears:** In rare cases, there may be tears in the perineal area or an episiotomy (cut) may be required.Cesarean Section: A Life-Saving Intervention

A cesarean section is the removal of the baby by cutting the abdominal wall and the uterus. This is not "delivery by order," but a serious abdominal surgery.Advantages:1.  **Planning:** You know the exact date of birth. you do not experience labor pains (in a planned surgery).
2.  **Life-saving:** It is the only way out in cases where natural birth is dangerous for the mother or the baby.
3.  **Painless process:** You do not feel any pain during the surgery (with spinal anesthesia).Disadvantages and Risks:  - **Long recovery period:** Full recovery can take 6-8 weeks. Walking, laughing, and lifting the baby are painful in the first days.
  - **Surgical risks:** There are risks of infection, bleeding, blood clots (thrombus), and damage to neighboring organs.
  - **Future pregnancies:** Because a scar remains on the uterus, risks in subsequent pregnancies (placenta accreta, uterine rupture) increase slightly.
  - **Baby's breathing:** Since there is no "squeezing" process, babies can sometimes have transient respiratory distress.When is a Cesarean "Mandatory"? (Medical Indications)

Sometimes you don't have a choice because the medical situation requires surgery. These cases are divided into two parts:1. Absolute Indications (Natural birth is impossible):  - **Placenta Previa:** The placenta completely covers the cervix.
  - **Baby's position:** If the baby is in a transverse lie (lying sideways).
  - **Umbilical cord prolapse:** If the cord falls into the canal before the baby.
  - **Risk of uterine rupture:** If the scar from previous surgeries is very thin.2. Relative or Emergency Indications (Arising during labor):  - **Fetal hypoxia:** The baby's heartbeat weakens and they are deprived of oxygen.
  - **Failure to progress:** There are contractions, but the cervix does not open.
  - **Large fetus and narrow pelvis:** If the baby's head is too large to pass through the mother's pelvis (clinically narrow pelvis)."I'm afraid, I want surgery" (Tokophobia)

Many women want a cesarean section simply because they are afraid of pain. However, remember that cesarean sections also have pain – it’s just that this pain starts **after** the birth and lasts longer. In natural birth, the pain ends the moment the baby is born.

If your fear is great:  - Talk to your doctor about **Epidural anesthesia** (painless birth).
  - Attend birth preparation courses or consult a psychologist. Knowledge reduces fear.The best delivery method is the **method that ensures the health of the mother and the baby**. This can sometimes be the natural way, and sometimes the operating table.

Do not force yourself to be a "hero," but at the same time, do not run to surgery with groundless fears. Trust your doctor and make the decision together.

You can use the **Anacan app** to prepare your birth plan, track your contractions, and be ready for both scenarios. Be reunited in good health\!

articles.title: False Labor or True Labor: How to Tell the Difference?
articles.excerpt: How to distinguish between Braxton Hicks (false labor) and real labor contractions? Learn when to go to the hospital by tracking the frequency, intensity, and location of contractions, along with other signs that labor has begun.
articles.content:
As the final weeks of pregnancy approach, every woman feels as if she is sitting on pins and needles. Every small tension in your abdomen or every pain in your lower back makes you wonder: *"Is this it? Is labor starting? Should I grab my bag?"*.

For first-time mothers in particular, confusing false labor pains with real labor is very common. Even experienced mothers can sometimes hesitate. These "practice contractions," known in medical terms as **Braxton Hicks**, prepare your body for the big day, but it is important to distinguish them from real contractions (to avoid rushing to the hospital for no reason\!).

In this article, we will explain how to correctly read the signals your body sends and how to distinguish between "False" and "Real" labor.What are False Labor Pains (Braxton Hicks)?

These contractions usually begin in the 3rd trimester of pregnancy (sometimes earlier). You can think of them as a "workout" for the uterus. The uterine muscles contract and relax, strengthening themselves for the upcoming marathon.

**How to recognize false labor pains?**  - **Irregularity:** There is no specific time interval between contractions. One comes now, another an hour later, and the next one tomorrow.
  - **Discomfort rather than pain:** You feel tightening or hardening in the front of your abdomen, but it is not unbearable pain.
  - **Temporary:** The contraction stops when you change your position (lying down, walking) or drink water.
  - **Does not intensify:** The intensity of the pain does not increase over time; on the contrary, it decreases.What are Real Labor Contractions like?

When real labor begins, an irreversible process starts in your body. The purpose of these contractions is to open the cervix and push the baby into the birth canal.

**Characteristics of real contractions:**  - **Regularity:** Contractions come at precise intervals like a clock (e.g., every 10 minutes).
  - **Intensifying:** Over time, contractions become both more painful and last longer (starting from 30 seconds and extending up to 1 minute).
  - **Location is different:** The pain usually **starts in the lower back** and spreads toward the front of the abdomen (as if a strong belt is tightening).
  - **Does not stop:** No matter how much you lie down or take a shower, the contractions do not cease."Test" methods to know the difference

If you are still not sure, try these simple tests:1.  **Movement test:** Walk around. If the pain decreases as you walk, it is false. If walking increases the pain or if you are in too much pain to walk, it is real.
2.  **Water test:** Drink a glass of water. Dehydration is a major cause of false labor pains. If it passes after drinking water, relax.
3.  **Shower test:** Take a warm (not hot) shower. Warm water relaxes the muscles. False labor will disappear in the shower, while real labor will continue.Other signs that labor has started

Contractions may not come alone. These signs also signal that the "big meeting" is approaching:  - **Show (Mucus plug):** The discharge of the mucus plug (slightly bloody or brown in color) that protects the cervix. This can indicate that labor is a few days or hours away.
  - **Water breaking:** Rupture of the amniotic sac. This may not be a "flood" like in the movies; sometimes it is just a leak. If your water has broken, you must **go to the hospital immediately**, even if there are no contractions (risk of infection\!).
  - **Diarrhea:** Before birth, the body releases prostaglandins to clear the intestines.When to go to the hospital? (The 5-1-1 Rule)

Unless your doctor has given you different instructions, follow the generally accepted **"5-1-1"** rule:  - Contractions occur every **5 minutes**.
  - Each contraction lasts at least **1 minute**.
  - This pattern has been continuing for **1 hour**.If you have established this rhythm, it is time to grab your bag and head to the maternity hospital!Note: If there is bleeding, if your water has broken, if the baby's movements have decreased, or if you simply feel unwell, consult a doctor immediately without waiting for contractions.

Contractions may seem scary, but they are actually your greatest helpers. Every contraction brings your baby a little closer to you. Trust your body; it knows what to do.

Don't waste time manually calculating the duration and interval of contractions. Press the **"Contraction Timer"** button in the **Anacan app**. The app will tell you whether the contractions are false or real and whether it is time to go to the hospital.

articles.title: Childbirth Package Prices in Baku 2026: Public vs. Private Clinic Comparison
articles.excerpt: What are the prices for natural birth and C-section in Baku in 2026? A price comparison of Liv Bona Dea, Leyla Medical, and other clinics. Information on free childbirth with Mandatory Health Insurance and services included in "Maternity Packages."
articles.content:
After the joy brought by the news of pregnancy comes the time to plan the family budget. The changing economic situation and inflation every year naturally affect the price of medical services. The question "How much does childbirth cost in Baku?" is one of the most searched topics by every future father and mother today.

Your options are wide: from completely free public services to premium clinics offering hotel comfort. But what are the real figures in 2026? What is the difference between a 1000 AZN package and a 3000 AZN package?

We have researched the latest market prices and the "behind-the-scenes" details of the packages for you.Option 1: State Maternity Hospitals (Free / MIS)

If your budget is limited or you simply do not want to spend a large amount on childbirth, state maternity hospitals (Perinatal Centers) are the best choice.  - **Price:** **0 AZN**.
  - **How does it work?** Within the framework of **Mandatory Health Insurance (MHI)** applied in Azerbaijan, pregnancy check-ups, natural birth, and cesarean section based on medical indications are completely free.
  - **What's included?** Stay of mother and child in the hospital, food, medicine supply, and initial vaccinations.
  - **Nuances:** A doctor on duty provides service to you within the "Services Envelope." If you want to choose a specific doctor, this may require additional (official or unofficial) costs. Wards are usually shared (2-4 people).Option 2: Private Clinics – 2026 Price Overview

Private clinics offer comfort, an individual approach, and freedom of doctor choice. Prices vary drastically depending on the prestige and location of the clinic.

Here are the **approximate** price ranges in popular clinics in Baku:| Segment     | Clinic Examples                | Natural Birth   | Cesarean Section |
| :---------- | :----------------------------- | :-------------- | :--------------- |
| **Premium** | Liv Bona Dea Hospital          | 1800 - 2500 AZN | 2500 - 3000+ AZN |
| **Medium**  | Baku Medical Plaza             | 1200 - 1300 AZN | 1400 - 1600 AZN  |
| **Medium**  | Leyla Medical Center           | 1100 - 1200 AZN | 1400 - 1500 AZN  |
| **Medium**  | Oksigen Clinic                 | 1000 - 1200 AZN | 1300 - 1400 AZN  |
| **Budget**  | Caspian International Hospital | 900 - 1000 AZN  | 1100 - 1200 AZN  |
| **Budget**  | German Hospital                | 900 - 1000 AZN  | 1100 - 1200 AZN  |
Note: Prices are approximate and may change depending on the doctor's academic degree (Associate Professor, Professor) and the type of ward chosen (VIP, Standard).What is usually included in a "Birth Package"?

When you pay 1200 AZN to a clinic, what do you actually get? A standard package usually includes the following:1.  **Birth process:** Operating room or delivery room costs.
2.  **Length of stay:** 1-2 days stay in a ward for natural birth, 2-3 days for cesarean section.
3.  **Nutrition:** 3-4 meals a day for the mother.
4.  **Baby care:** Initial neonatologist examination, vaccinations (Hepatitis B and Tuberculosis), blood group analysis.
5.  **Medicines:** Painkillers during and after birth.Hidden Costs: What should you consider?

To avoid surprises at the checkout, ask these questions in advance:  - **Epidural Anesthesia (Painless birth):** In many clinics, this is not included in the package and may require an additional **100-200 AZN**.
  - **Doctor's fee:** The fees of some "Star" doctors are calculated additionally to the standard package.
  - **Extra night:** If health problems arise or you simply want to stay longer, there may be a charge of **80-150 AZN** for each night.
  - **Twins:** The price for two babies is usually **20-30% higher** than the standard package.
  - **Neonatal Intensive Care:** Is the baby's stay in an incubator included in the package? This can be the largest expense item.
  - **Partner's stay:** An additional fee may be required for the father to stay in the ward and for his meals.How to manage the budget?1.  **Early booking:** Some clinics offer a discount (Early Bird) to those who sign a contract in the early months of pregnancy.
2.  **Insurance:** If you have **Voluntary Health Insurance (VHI)** from your workplace, check if it covers pregnancy and childbirth costs. (For example, *PASHA Insurance* makes limited payments in some packages).
3.  **Campaigns:** Follow the discount campaigns of clinics on holidays (Novruz, March 8).An expensive clinic does not always mean a "better birth." Most important is your doctor's professionalism and the clinic's resuscitation capabilities. When calculating your budget, consider not only the price of birth but also the funds needed for the first months after birth (diapers, clothes, doctor visits).

To find the most suitable option for yourself and calculate your expenses, you can use the **"Birth Calculator" in the Anacan app**.

articles.title: Choosing a Maternity Hospital and Doctor in Baku: Key Considerations
articles.excerpt: What to consider when choosing a maternity hospital? Public or private clinic? What is included in maternity packages? A detailed guide on doctor selection, neonatal intensive care, and childbirth prices.
articles.content:
One of the first questions that comes to every mother-to-be's mind immediately after seeing a positive pregnancy test result is: *"Where and with whom will I give birth to my baby?"*. As the number of maternity hospitals and private clinics in Baku increases, making a choice becomes even more difficult. On one hand, the accessibility of state maternity hospitals, and on the other, the hotel-like comfort of private clinics... But what is most important? Marble floors or a professional team? In this article, we will set aside advertising slogans and explore the criteria that will help you make the right decision for both your health and your budget.Step 1: State or Private? Differences and Realities

This is the first decision you need to make. Both have their own advantages and disadvantages.State Maternity Hospitals (Perinatal Centers)  - **Advantages:** Birth and cesarean section operations are **free of charge** as they are covered by Mandatory Health Insurance (MHI). Large maternity hospitals (e.g., Research Institute of Obstetrics and Gynecology - "6th Maternity Hospital") have experienced doctors and strong intensive care units.
  - **Disadvantages:** Ward conditions may not be as luxurious as in private clinics. There may be multi-person wards. Doctor choice is not always possible (the doctor on duty may admit you).Private Clinics  - **Advantages:** Single, comfortable wards, the possibility to choose a doctor, a more loyal approach to the father's participation in the birth (partner birth), friendly staff, and high service levels.
  - **Disadvantages:** High financial cost. Prices can range from 1000 AZN to 3000 AZN.Step 2: How to choose a doctor?

Clinic walls will not deliver your baby; the doctor will. Therefore, your main focus should be the doctor.  - **Recommendations:** Your friends' advice is important, but not enough. Do not blindly believe "advertising" posts on social media. Read real patient reviews (the "Doctors Catalog" in the **Anacan app** is ideal for this).
  - **Approach to birth:** Is the doctor a supporter of natural birth, or do they immediately suggest a cesarean? Are they prone to performing an "incision" (episiotomy)? Do not hesitate to ask these questions at the first meeting.
  - **Accessibility:** If your water breaks at 3 AM, will they answer the phone? Will they attend the birth themselves, or will they hand it over to the doctor on duty?Step 3: "Golden Rules" for Clinic Selection (Checklist)

Be sure to ask these questions when you go for a clinic tour:1. Neonatal Intensive Care (THE MOST IMPORTANT POINT!)

Marble floors and delicious food are nice, but they don't save lives.  - **Question:** "If a problem arises with my baby (premature birth, respiratory problem), will they need to be moved to another hospital, or is there an **Incubator (Küvəz)** and an intensive care unit here?"
  - If there is no intensive care, remove that clinic from your list. You don't want to lose that "golden hour" on the road in an emergency.2. What is included in the Birth Package?

Read the contract carefully. Do not be deceived by a 1200 AZN "Package"; additional costs may arise later.  - **Clarify:**
      - Is anesthesia (Epidural) included in the price?
      - How many days can you stay in the ward? (What is the fee for an extra day?)
      - Are the baby's initial examinations (blood group, jaundice test, hearing test) and vaccinations (Hepatitis B, TB) in the package?
      - Is an additional payment required for the father's stay or food?3. Delivery Room and Ward Conditions  - Does the birth take place in a ward or a general delivery room? (In private clinics, labor, delivery, and recovery are usually in the same room, which is very convenient).
  - Is there a shower and toilet in the ward?
  - How is the heating system?4. Partner Birth (Your partner's participation)

If you want your partner to be with you, learn the rules. Some clinics may require extra payment or specific tests (Chest X-ray, etc.).Step 4: Be ready for "Plan B"

Even if you have chosen your doctor and clinic, always have a backup option.  - Your doctor may be on vacation or ill. Do you know the doctor who will replace them?
  - There may be no room in your chosen clinic (though this is very rare).Choosing a maternity hospital is not just choosing a building. It is the place where your baby will open their eyes to life and where you will be born as a mother. Feeling safe and comfortable there is more important than anything else.

Don't rush to decide. Compare prices in the "Clinics" section of the **Anacan app**, read the reviews, and choose the place that feels right to you.

We wish you a healthy and comfortable birth!

articles.title: Hospital Bag: What Should You Take With You? (Full List)
articles.excerpt: When should the hospital bag be prepared? What should be included in the hospital bag for mother and baby? A complete list of documents, hygiene products, and essentials not to be forgotten.
articles.content:
After passing the 30th week of pregnancy, every mother-to-be is overwhelmed by the "Nesting instinct." The desire to clean the house, prepare the nursery, and most importantly — pack that famous **Hospital Bag** — reaches its peak.

Packing the bag on time and correctly will save you from unnecessary stress. When contractions start, you do not want to be thinking, "I wonder if I took my toothbrush?" So, what should be put in the bag? Which items are essential, and which are just extra weight?

Taking into account the realities of Azerbaijani maternity hospitals, we have prepared the most optimal list for you.When to prepare the bag?

The ideal time is **36-37 weeks** of pregnancy.  - **Twins:** It is better to have your bag ready at 32-34 weeks.
  - **Advice:** Keep the bag near the door or in the trunk of the car. Also, show your partner the location of the bag and its contents.Section 1: Documents (The Most Important Part)

Keep these in a separate folder for hospital admission and baby registration:1.  **ID card:** Both yours and your partner's.
2.  **Exchange card (Pregnancy card):** The booklet given by the women's consultation clinic containing all your test results. Without this, they may place you in the infectious disease ward.
3.  **Marriage certificate:** May be needed to register the baby's birth certificate and "Child money" (600 AZN).
4.  **Medical insurance or Contract:** If you are giving birth in a private clinic (e.g., *Baku Medical Plaza*, *Leyla Medical Center*), the contract documents.Section 2: Essentials for the Mother

These items are indispensable for you to feel comfortable.For the Delivery Process and Ward:  - **Nightgown or Pajamas (2-3 sets):** Choose models with front buttons or special openings for breastfeeding. It is important that they are natural cotton.
  - **Robe:** To wear when walking in the corridor or when visitors arrive.
  - **Slippers (Slides):** Washable rubber slippers (also comfortable for the shower).
  - **Socks:** Feet often get cold during and after labor.
  - **Phone and Charger:** With a long cord (the outlet may be far from the bed).Hygiene and Care:  - **Postpartum pads:** Regular pads may not be enough. Buy special urological or postpartum pads from the pharmacy.
  - **Disposable underwear:** Very practical to throw away when soiled.
  - **Nursing bra:** 2 pieces.
  - **Nipple cream (Lanolin):** To prevent sores and cracks in the first days of breastfeeding (safe for the baby, no need to wash off).
  - **Breast pads:** To prevent milk leakage.
  - **Hygiene bag:** Toothbrush, toothpaste, soap, shampoo, comb, moisturizer, deodorant.Section 3: Essentials for the Baby

The baby's skin is very sensitive, so do not forget to wash the clothes beforehand with "baby powder" and iron them.  - **Diapers (Pampers):** "Newborn" size (size 1 or 2-5 kg). 1 pack (20-30 pieces) is enough for your hospital stay.
  - **Wet wipes:** Alcohol-free, paraben-free, and fragrance-free (water-based).
  - **Diaper cream:** Zinc-based cream (against rashes).
  - **Clothing sets (3-4 sets):**
      - Body (onesie) – with bottom snaps.
      - Romper (jumpsuit with legs).
      - Thin hat and mittens (so the baby doesn't scratch themselves).
      - Socks.
  - **Swaddle or thin blanket:** According to the season (cotton or flannel).
  - **Discharge set (Outfit):** A decorative or simple set for wearing when going home from the hospital.Section 4: Food (Snacks)

Hospital food may not always be available when you want it.  - **Water:** Water in small bottles (it is difficult to drink from a large bottle while lying down).
  - **Energy:** Dried fruit, walnuts/hazelnuts, crackers, chocolate (with doctor's permission).What NOT to take?  - **Valuable jewelry:** Risk of loss.
  - **Tight clothes:** You will not fit back into your pre-pregnancy jeans immediately after leaving the hospital. Take your maternity clothes.
  - **Lots of makeup:** Minimum cosmetics for the discharge day is enough.Checklist – Download Now!

Don't want to deal with a paper list? The **Anacan app** has a **"Smart Hospital Bag"** function prepared for you.1.  Mark items on the list one by one (tick).
2.  Add your own items.
3.  See the completion percentage of the bag.If everything is ready, take a deep breath. The big meeting is almost here!

articles.title: Flying While Pregnant: Is It Safe and Until What Week?
articles.excerpt: Is it safe to fly during pregnancy? Up to which week do airlines (AZAL, THY) allow travel? "Fit to Fly" certificates, airport scanners, and golden rules for preventing thrombosis during flight.
articles.content:
Pregnancy does not mean completely changing your lifestyle. Whether it's a business trip or a final "Babymoon" before the baby is born, the desire to travel by plane is completely normal. However, before clicking the "Confirm" button when buying a ticket, a hesitation arises within you: *"Will the pressure harm the baby?", "What if my contractions start in the air?"*. The airplane is one of the safest modes of transport for pregnant women, but it has certain "buts." In this article, we have gathered airline rules, doctors' recommendations, and the secrets of traveling comfortably above the clouds for you.General question: Do Pressure and Radiation harm the baby?

Many expectant mothers fear changes in cabin pressure and cosmic radiation.  - **Cabin pressure:** Modern passenger planes are airtight (hermetic), and the internal pressure is regulated. Although this is slightly higher than sea level, it does not negatively affect the baby's oxygen supply for a healthy pregnancy.
  - **Radiation:** Because the plane flies high, the level of cosmic radiation is slightly higher than on the ground. However, for occasional flights, this dose is **negligible** and does not harm the fetus. (Risk exists only for flight attendants and pilots who fly every day).The "Golden Era" for Flight: 2nd Trimester

Doctors state that the ideal time for travel is between the **14th and 28th weeks** of pregnancy (second trimester).  - **Why?** The morning sickness and fatigue of the first trimester are behind you, and the risk of miscarriage has significantly decreased. At the same time, your belly is not yet large enough to hinder movement, and the risk of premature birth is low.Airline Rules: Who is allowed, and When?

Although rules vary from company to company (e.g., AZAL, Turkish Airlines), international standards (IATA) are usually as follows:For single fetus (one baby) pregnancy:  - **Up to the 28th week:** A doctor's certificate is not required; you can fly comfortably.
  - **Between 28-35 weeks:** A **"Fit to Fly"** certificate from a doctor is required to be allowed on the flight. The certificate must state the week of pregnancy and the phrase "no obstacle to flight" (usually obtained within 7 days before the flight).
  - **After the 36th week:** Even with a doctor's permission, you are usually **not accepted** onto the plane. The reason is simple: no company wants to take the risk of birth on board.For twin (multiple) pregnancy:

The periods are shorter. Usually, flights are prohibited **after the 32nd week**.Important: Before buying a ticket, be sure to read the "Pregnant passengers" section on the official website of your chosen airline.Airport Scanners: Can you pass through?

Security checks at the airport are another source of fear.  - **Metal detectors (Frames):** These work with a magnetic field and are completely safe.
  - **Body scanners (Millimeter wave):** They do not emit radiation, work with radio waves, and are considered safe.
  - **X-Ray:** Only for bags\! Never put your hand or body inside the belt where the bags pass.If you are still concerned, you can inform the staff that you are pregnant and request a manual check.The Biggest Risk: Deep Vein Thrombosis (DVT)

Pregnancy increases the blood's ability to clot. Sitting motionless for a long time on a plane increases the risk of blood clots (thrombi) forming in the legs.

**How to protect yourself?**1.  **Compression socks:** Consult your doctor and wear anti-varicose socks.
2.  **Movement:** Get up and walk along the cabin every hour.
3.  **Exercises in place:** Rotate your feet in a circular motion while sitting, and raise and lower your heels.
4.  **Water regimen:** Airplane air is dry. Drink plenty of water to prevent the blood from thickening. Stay away from coffee and tea.Tips for a comfortable flight  - **Seat selection:** Choose an aisle seat. This is convenient for frequent trips to the toilet and stretching your legs.
  - **Seat belt:** Fasten the belt **under** your belly (over the hip bones), not over it.
  - **Insurance:** Check whether your travel insurance covers pregnancy-related expenses.Who should not fly? (Contraindications)

Your doctor will not allow the flight in the following cases:  - If there is a diagnosis of placenta previa.
  - If there is a risk of preeclampsia (high blood pressure).
  - If there is cervical shortening or risk of premature birth.
  - If there is a suspicion of water breaking or bleeding.
  - Severe anemia (if hemoglobin is very low).Traveling during pregnancy is possible and even necessary (it will be hard to find time for this after the baby is born!). It just requires a bit more planning and caution.

Before the flight, be sure to meet with your doctor, get your "Fit to Fly" certificate, and calculate your pregnancy week accurately in the **Anacan app** so that you don't face surprises at the airport. Safe travels\!

articles.title: Taking Medication During Pregnancy: What to Know About Paracetamol and Antibiotics
articles.excerpt: Which medicines can you take during pregnancy? Is paracetamol safe? Essential information on antibiotic use, risks of ibuprofen, and FDA categories. A medication guide to protect yourself and your baby.
articles.content:
Before pregnancy, when we had a headache or felt a cold coming on, our hand would reach for the medicine cabinet without thinking. However, after receiving the news of pregnancy, the situation changes. Now we look at every pill as a "potential enemy."

On one hand, there is unbearable pain or high fever, and on the other hand, the fear: *"If I take medicine, will it harm my baby?"* This dilemma leaves many expectant mothers helpless. Sometimes the fear is so strong that women even refuse essential treatments prescribed by a doctor.

So, where does the truth lie? Which medicines are a "green light" and which are strictly "prohibited"? Let's look at the medical facts about the most commonly used medications during pregnancy.The Golden Rule: Say NO to self-medication!

Before starting the article, let's recall the most important rule: **Do not take any medication (even herbal ones) during pregnancy without consulting your doctor.** A medicine that worked well for a neighbor may not be suitable for your week of pregnancy or your condition.Paracetamol: The "Savior" of Pregnant Women

The most recommended medication for pain relief and fever reduction during pregnancy is **Paracetamol** (Panadol, Efferalgan, etc.).Why is it considered safe?

Medical research shows that when taken in recommended doses, paracetamol does not negatively affect fetal development. Although it crosses the placenta, it has no toxic effects.When should it be taken?  - **High fever:** A fever above 38°C during pregnancy is more dangerous for the baby than the medication itself. High fever can speed up the fetus's heart rate and damage protein structures. Therefore, it is **essential** to reduce the fever with paracetamol.
  - **Pain:** Instead of enduring head, tooth, or muscle pain, taking paracetamol is better for reducing stress hormones.Attention: Even though it is safe, it should not be taken "like candy." Use the lowest possible dose for the shortest possible duration.Antibiotics: Friend or Foe?

The idea that "antibiotics are harmful" is deeply rooted in our society. However, untreated infections during pregnancy (e.g., kidney infection, pneumonia, sexual infections) are far riskier for the baby than antibiotics. Infection can lead to premature birth, premature rupture of membranes, and fetal growth restriction.

Doctors prescribe only **safe group** antibiotics to pregnant women:

✅ **Approved Antibiotics:**  - **Penicillin group:** (e.g., Amoxicillin, Ampicillin). This is the most widely used and safest group.
  - **Macrolides:** (e.g., Erythromycin, Azithromycin). Prescribed for those with penicillin allergies.
  - **Cephalosporins:** (e.g., Cephalexin).❌ **Prohibited Antibiotics:**  - **Tetracyclines:** Impair the baby's bone development and cause permanent yellow staining on teeth.
  - **Streptomycin:** Can damage the fetus's auditory nerve (risk of deafness).
  - **Chloramphenicol:** Can cause "Gray Baby Syndrome."**Conclusion:** If your doctor has prescribed an antibiotic, it means the benefit far outweighs the risk. Be sure to complete the course.Ibuprofen and Aspirin: Why should we be careful?

One of the most popular medications for headaches, **Ibuprofen (Nurofen)**, and other non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) are **prohibited during pregnancy, especially in the 3rd trimester (after the 28th week)**.  - **Risk:** These drugs can cause an important vessel in the baby's heart (Ductus Arteriosus) to close prematurely, which creates serious heart and lung problems. It can also lead to a decrease in amniotic fluid (oligohydramnios).
  - **Aspirin:** Can only be taken if prescribed by a doctor in a specific dose (e.g., "Cardioaspirin" against the risk of preeclampsia). Self-use as a painkiller creates a risk of bleeding.What to do during Cold and Flu?

"Packet powders" purchased from the pharmacy (Teraflu, Fervex, etc.) during seasonal illnesses are not suitable for pregnant women because they contain vasoconstrictors.

**Safe alternatives:**  - **For nasal congestion:** Sea water sprays (Aquamaris, etc.) are completely safe. Drops containing Xylometazoline can only be used with doctor's permission for a short period (max. 3 days).
  - **For sore throat:** Gargling with salt water, warm milk, and honey.
  - **For cough:** Herbal syrups (with a doctor's prescription).Drug Categories in Pregnancy (FDA)

You may come across these letters when reading a medicine box. This is the classification by the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA):  - **Category A:** Tested on humans, completely safe (e.g., Folic acid).
  - **Category B:** Harmless in animals, insufficient research in humans, but considered safe (e.g., Paracetamol, Amoxicillin).
  - **Category C:** Shown negative effects in animals, data in humans is scarce. Used only if benefits outweigh risks.
  - **Category D:** Risk to the human fetus is proven. Used only in life-threatening situations.
  - **Category X:** Strictly prohibited (Teratogenic). Causes serious harm to the fetus.Pregnancy does not mean remaining "defenseless" against illnesses. Modern medicine provides us with enough safe tools to both heal the mother and protect the baby.

If you are hesitant about taking any medication, download the **Anacan app**. You can instantly check the status of hundreds of medicines during pregnancy (Green/Yellow/Red) in the "Safety Lookup" section of the app.

Stay healthy so that your baby grows up healthy too!

articles.title: Benefits of eating pomegranate and dates during pregnancy: Does it really make labor easier?
articles.excerpt: Does eating dates during pregnancy speed up labor? What are the benefits of pomegranate for anemia and placental health? Scientific evidence on nutrition in the final weeks and how to facilitate childbirth.
articles.content:
As the final weeks of pregnancy approach, every expectant mother's greatest wish is the same: *"I wish my delivery would be easy and fast"*. At this stage, the advice you most likely hear from grandmothers, neighbors, and internet forums is this: **"Eat dates, so your delivery goes smooth like oil"** or **"Eat pomegranates to increase your blood count and have strength"**.

Can pomegranates and dates, which are an integral part of Azerbaijani cuisine and culture, really be considered "superfoods" for pregnant women? Or is this just a myth? Fortunately, there are serious scientific studies conducted on this topic.

Let's explore the real effects of these two delicious fruits on the birthing process and the baby's health.Dates: Nature's "Natural Oxytocin"?

Since ancient times, dates (especially Medina dates or Iranian dates) have been used to alleviate labor pains. Modern medicine confirms this ancient knowledge.What do the scientific proofs say?

Clinical studies (e.g., *Journal of Obstetrics and Gynaecology*) show that women who eat **6 dates per day** in the last 4 weeks of pregnancy (from the 36th week onwards):1.  **Cervical dilation happens faster:** The cervical dilation of women who eat dates is greater upon admission to the hospital compared to those who do not.
2.  **Reduced need for artificial labor induction:** The probability of labor starting naturally increases, and the need for medical intervention (induction) decreases.
3.  **Labor duration is shortened:** It has been observed that the latent phase (the initial stage of labor) lasts for a shorter period.**The Reason:** Substances in dates act similarly to the hormone oxytocin, helping uterine muscles contract more effectively. Additionally, dates are a **natural energy** source you will need during labor.Attention: Dates are high in sugar! If you have gestational diabetes, do not eat this many dates without consulting your doctor.Pomegranate: Azerbaijan's "Red Gold" and Pregnancy

Our country is a pomegranate paradise, and this fruit is a true treasure for pregnant women. While pomegranates do not have direct "labor-inducing" properties like dates, they are indispensable for preparing you and your baby for delivery.1. Iron Depot and Fighting Anemia

Anemia is a common occurrence during pregnancy. Pomegranates are rich in iron and help increase hemoglobin levels in the blood. Having strong blood counts is essential to be ready for blood loss during delivery.2. Placenta Protector

Pomegranate juice is packed with powerful antioxidants (polyphenols). Research shows that these antioxidants protect the placenta from damage and improve blood flow to the baby. This is particularly important for reducing the risk of **intrauterine growth restriction**.3. Vitamin K and Bone Health

Pomegranates are rich in Vitamin K, which is vital for both your and your baby's bones. Vitamin K is also essential for blood clotting, which is important during the postpartum recovery period.4. Against Cramps

Thanks to its potassium content, pomegranates help reduce leg cramps that may bother you at night during the final months of pregnancy.How and When to Consume?

To get the maximum benefit from these advantages, you can follow these rules:  - **Dates:** 4-6 pieces per day starting from the **36th week** of pregnancy. You can consume them with walnuts, milk, or in a smoothie.
  - **Pomegranate:** Beneficial during **all stages** of pregnancy. During the season, it is ideal to eat half a cup of pomegranate seeds or drink fresh-pressed juice (1 cup per day) every day.
      - *Note:* Pomegranate juice can cause constipation, so do not forget to drink plenty of water. Also, those with heartburn (reflux) should be cautious.Our grandmothers were right! Science proves that dates can physiologically ease the birthing process, while pomegranates prepare your body for this process.

Of course, simply eating dates does not guarantee a painless birth, but it is a natural and delicious support tool. If you do not have sugar problems, don't forget to put a box of dates and a bottle of pomegranate juice in your hospital bag – you will also need them to restore your energy after birth!

**Want to track your nutrition?**
Download the **Anacan app** to plan your daily menu and view the "Safe Foods" list.
